content: 1. Ketoconazole increases the levels or effects of ritonavir by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Close monitoring is required, and therapy adjustments may be necessary. 2. Ketoconazole also increases the levels or effects of lopinavir through the same mechanism (CYP3A4 inhibition). Therapy adjustments and close monitoring are recommended. 3. Ketoconazole increases ritonavir levels via P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter inhibition. Therapy adjustments and close monitoring are advised. 4. Ritonavir increases ketoconazole levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. This interaction is considered minor, but close monitoring is still recommended. 5. Ritonavir increases lacosamide levels through pharmacodynamic synergism, potentially increasing toxicity. Therapy adjustments, close monitoring, or alternative treatments should be considered. 6. Lopinavir increases lacosamide levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy adjustments and close monitoring are necessary. 7. Ritonavir and lacosamide mutually increase each other's levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Dose reduction of lacosamide should be considered when co-administered with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. 8. Ritonavir and lamivudine both increase the risk of immune reconstitution syndrome. Caution and close monitoring are required. 9. Lopinavir decreases lamotrigine levels by increasing its metabolism, potentially reducing lamotrigine levels by up to 50%. Caution and close monitoring are necessary. 10. Ritonavir also decreases lamotrigine levels by increasing its metabolism. Dose adjustments of lamotrigine are recommended when starting, stopping, or changing ritonavir doses. 11. Ritonavir increases lansoprazole levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. This interaction is minor, but its clinical significance is unknown. Close monitoring is advised. 12. Lapatinib increases ritonavir levels via P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter inhibition and CYP3A4 metabolism inhibition. Close monitoring is required. 13. Lopinavir increases lapatinib levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. This interaction is serious, and alternative treatments should be considered. 14. Ritonavir increases lapatinib levels through CYP3A4 inhibition. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 15. Ritonavir increases larotrectinib levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. If co-administration is unavoidable, reduce the larotrectinib dose by 50%. 16. Lopinavir increases larotrectinib levels through CYP3A4 inhibition. Avoid or use alternative drugs. If co-administration is unavoidable, reduce the larotrectinib dose by 50%. 17. Larotrectinib increases lopinavir levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Lenacapavir may increase CYP3A4 substrate levels initiated within 9 months after the last subcutaneous dose, increasing the risk of adverse reactions. 27.
